class.name: PhysXLiveWater3D
class.brief_description: Live shallow water over any ground: it flows downhill, fills hollows, floods and drains.
class.description: A square of [member size] over the ground at [member cell_size], centred on the node and aligned with its axes. The ground is measured once by ray casts down through every cell (static bodies on [member ground_collision_mask], so terrain, rocks, walls and buildings all count; a cell with nothing under it is a drain). Water comes from [member sources], rain ([member rain_rate], plus the active [code]WeatherMap3D[/code]'s with [member rain_from_weather]) and [method add_water], and can start filled up to [member fill_height]. It leaves over the open edges ([member open_edges]) and by soaking in ([member infiltration_rate]). Solved on the CPU every physics tick with virtual pipes (O'Brien and Hodgins 1995; Mei, Decaudin and Hu 2007): per cell a depth and four outflows, each accelerated by the difference in surface height to the neighbour, slowed by [member friction], and scaled down together when they would take more water than the cell holds. Volume is kept exactly, depth never goes negative, and fronts wet and dry ground without special cases. Substeps keep each step under the speed of the fastest gravity wave (at most 16 a tick). Drawn with [PhysXRiver3D]'s surface (clear water, shadows, sky and sun reflections, white water where it runs fast and shoots, and the path tracer's refracting medium): a vertex per cell, triangles only where water is. The waterline falls between a wet cell and a dry one. Changing [member size], [member cell_size], [member ground_collision_mask] or the fill, or moving the node, starts over; [method update_ground] measures the ground again and keeps the water (a dam removed).

method.name: add_water
method.description: Pours [param volume] m³ evenly over the cells within [param radius] m of [param position] (world space).

method.name: get_cost_ms
method.description: CPU time the last physics tick spent on the solver and the surface mesh, in milliseconds.

method.name: get_total_volume
method.description: Water held in the area, in m³.

method.name: get_volume_out
method.description: Water that has left over the open edges or into drains since the last start, in m³.

method.name: get_water_material
method.description: The surface's material (the river's shader); its parameters can be changed.

method.name: reset
method.description: Measures the ground again and starts over (dry, or filled to [member fill_height]).

method.name: sample_depth
method.description: Water depth in m at a world point; 0 where dry or outside the area.

method.name: sample_flow
method.description: Depth-averaged velocity of the water at a world point, in world space (m/s).

method.name: sample_height
method.description: World height of the water's surface at a point (the ground's where dry), or NaN outside the area.

method.name: update_ground
method.description: Measures the ground again at the next physics tick, keeping the water where it is: call it after the ground changes (a wall or dam removed, a crater). Where the ground rose, it takes the water's place.

members.member: Size of a cell in m. At most 1024 x 1024 cells; a larger [member size] / [member cell_size] is clamped.
Starts with water up to [member fill_height] wherever the ground is below it (within [member fill_rect] when set): a pond, or a reservoir behind a dam.
Local height the area starts filled to, with [member fill_enabled].
Local XZ rectangle the fill is limited to (x, z, width, depth); empty fills the whole area.
Speed in m/s where white water starts. It also needs the flow to be shooting (Froude number well past 1) and at least a few centimetres deep.
How fast the pipes' flow is slowed, per second: the ground's drag on the water.
Physics layers measured as ground. Only static bodies count.
Water soaking into the ground everywhere, in mm/h.
Water flows out over the area's edges (and is gone, counted in [method get_volume_out]). Off, the edges are walls.
Adds the active [code]WeatherMap3D[/code]'s rain at the node's position to [member rain_rate].
Rain falling on the whole area, in mm/h.
Sky and sun reflections and clear water in the rasterizer, as [member PhysXRiver3D.raster_reflections].
Steps the water every physics tick (not in the editor). Off, it holds still.
Width and depth of the area in m (local X and Z).
Radius in m each of [member sources] pours over.
Springs and inflows: local position in xyz, inflow in m³/s in w.
